sections.title: Chapter One - Smiling Jesus
sections.html:
CHAPTER ONE

Smiling Jesus


JESUS SMILED A lot.
Not because everything was easy.
But because he loved people.

He smiled when someone shared their snack.
He smiled when kids danced in the dirt.
He probably even smiled when someone made a funny face during prayer.

He didn’t smile to look polite.
He smiled because he meant it.

Happy Jesus smiled like the world was still good —
Because deep down,
He believed it was.

sections.title: Chapter Two - The Time He Shared His Lunch
sections.html:
CHAPTER TWO

The Time He Shared His Lunch


ONE TIME, A little boy brought Jesus his lunch.
It was just a few fish and some bread.
Not enough to feed a crowd. Not even close.

But Jesus didn’t laugh.
He didn’t say, “That’s not enough.”
He said, “Perfect.”

He broke the bread, blessed it, and passed it around.
And somehow…
Everyone ate.

Thousands of people.
Full hearts. Full bellies.
All from one small lunch someone was willing to share.

Jesus didn’t need a feast.
He just needed someone willing to give what they had.

sections.title: Chapter Three - People Got Mad
sections.html:
CHAPTER THREE

People Got Mad


SOME PEOPLE DIDN’T like Jesus.
Not because he was mean.
But because he was too kind.

He let everyone sit with him —
Poor people, sick people, people who messed up.
People who didn’t follow the rules.

That made the rule-makers angry.
They said he was being too soft.
Too free.
Too forgiving.

But Jesus didn’t flinch.
He didn’t argue.
He just kept being love anyway.

And sometimes, love makes people mad.
But he never stopped loving.

Not even once.

sections.title: Chapter Four - Jesus and the Weird Kids
sections.html:
CHAPTER FOUR

Jesus and the Weird Kids


JESUS LIKED THE weird kids.
The quiet ones.
The loud ones.
The ones who drew pictures during serious talks.

He liked the kids who asked too many questions.
The ones who made up silly songs.
The ones who didn’t always sit still.

He saw their sparkle.
He saw their heart.
He saw their realness.

And while other people said, “Be normal,”
Jesus said,

“Come sit by me.”

Because Jesus didn’t want perfect kids.
He wanted the ones being themselves.

sections.title: Chapter Five - He Sat With Everyone
sections.html:
CHAPTER FIVE

He Sat With Everyone


JESUS DIDN’T HAVE a favorites list.
He didn’t make charts.
He didn’t care who had the best clothes or the cleanest hands.

He sat with people who were rich.
He sat with people who were poor.
He sat with people who were loud, tired, silly, serious, sick, scared, quiet, forgotten.

If there was space on the ground,
He’d sit there too.

He didn’t ask, “Are you good enough?”
He just made sure you knew you belonged.

Everyone had a place near Jesus.
Even you.

sections.title: Chapter Six - No Gold Stars
sections.html:
CHAPTER SIX

No Gold Stars


JESUS DIDN’T HAND out gold stars.
He wasn’t keeping score.
He didn’t say, “Be the best or else.”

He cared more about hearts than charts.

Some people prayed fancy.
Some gave big gifts.
Some talked loud about how holy they were.

Jesus nodded.
Then he sat beside the quiet kid in the back
who gave someone a hug when no one was looking.

He didn’t say, “You’re better.”
He said, “That… was love.”

No gold star could ever mean more than that.

sections.title: Chapter Seven - Rules Are Fine, Love Is Better
sections.html:
CHAPTER SEVEN

Rules Are Fine, Love Is Better


RULES ARE FINE.
They help us stay safe.
They help us take turns.
They help us know what to do next.

Jesus didn’t hate rules.
He just didn’t worship them.

Some people followed every single rule —
but forgot to be kind.

And Jesus?
He picked kindness every time.

He said love was the biggest rule.
The one that wrapped around all the others
like a big soft blanket.

If it isn’t loving,
Jesus probably wouldn’t call it a rule at all.

sections.title: Chapter Eight - The Guy Who Yelled Got a Hug
sections.html:
CHAPTER EIGHT

The Guy Who Yelled Got a Hug


ONE DAY, A man yelled at Jesus.
He said mean things.
Loud things.
Scary things.

Everyone waited to see what Jesus would do.
Would he yell back?
Would he make the man go away?

But Jesus didn’t yell.
He didn’t shame.
He didn’t punish.

He looked at the man,
really looked.

Then he hugged him.

Because sometimes, when someone yells…
what they really need
is to feel safe enough to stop.

sections.title: Chapter Nine - Jesus Walked Everywhere
sections.html:
CHAPTER NINE

Jesus Walked Everywhere


JESUS COULD’VE FLOWN.
He could’ve teleported.
He could’ve ridden a glowing horse with rocket sandals.

But he didn’t.

He walked.
Everywhere.

It took longer.
It made his feet dirty.
Sometimes he got tired.

But walking let him meet people.
Talk to them.
Listen to their stories.

Jesus didn’t rush past life.
He walked with it.
One step at a time.

sections.title: Chapter Ten - He Wasn’t in a Rush
sections.html:
CHAPTER TEN

He Wasn’t in a Rush


JESUS NEVER HURRIED.

He didn’t tap his foot.
He didn’t say, “Come on, come on.”
He didn’t roll his eyes when someone took a little longer.

He moved slow enough to notice the hurting.
He paused when someone needed a breath.
He stayed longer when someone felt alone.

While everyone else chased the next big thing,
Jesus stayed right here.

Right now.
With whoever needed him most.

Because love doesn’t rush.
It waits.

sections.title: Chapter Eleven - Big Powers, Small Moments
sections.html:
CHAPTER ELEVEN

Big Powers, Small Moments


JESUS HAD BIG powers.
Like, really big.

He could calm storms.
Heal pain.
Feed a crowd with a lunchbox.

But most of the time?
He just sat with someone who was sad.
Listened to someone who was scared.
Laughed at a really bad joke.

He didn’t need thunder and lightning.
He just needed love.

Because the biggest power Jesus had…
was showing up when it mattered most.

sections.title: Chapter Twelve - Happy Jesus Forgives Fast
sections.html:
CHAPTER TWELVE

Happy Jesus Forgives Fast


JESUS DIDN’T STAY mad.
Even when someone hurt him.
Even when they lied, or yelled, or ran away.

He felt it, sure.
But then he let it go.

Not because he forgot —
but because he loved more than he hurt.

He forgave before people even said sorry.
He forgave while they were still being mean.

Happy Jesus didn’t wait for perfect.
He forgave fast,
so love could come back sooner.

sections.title: Chapter Thirteen - He Didn’t Kick Anyone Out
sections.html:
CHAPTER THIRTEEN

He Didn’t Kick Anyone Out


JESUS DIDN’T LOCK the doors.
He didn’t say, “You’re too late.”
He didn’t ask for a checklist before letting someone sit with him.

People messed up.
He still made room.
People doubted him.
He still offered bread.
People walked away.
He still waved when they passed by again.

Happy Jesus didn’t guard the gate.
He opened it.

Because love doesn’t lock people out.
It says, “You still belong.”

CHAPTER FOURTEEN

Sometimes He Needed Quiet, Too


JESUS LOVED PEOPLE.
But sometimes, he got tired.

So he went up a hill.
Or sat by the water.
Or found a quiet place to pray.

He didn’t disappear forever.
He just needed space to feel his own heart again.

Happy Jesus wasn’t a superhero.
He was a human, too.
And humans need quiet to stay soft.

If Jesus needed breaks,
You’re allowed to take them too.

CHAPTER FIFTEEN

Jesus Would’ve Played Tag


JESUS DIDN’T JUST preach.
He played.

He would’ve run in the grass.
He would’ve laughed when you almost tagged him.
He might’ve even let you win.

He liked joy.
He liked friends.
He liked moments that made hearts feel free.

If someone fell down,
He’d help them up —
then ask if they wanted another turn.

Happy Jesus wasn’t above fun.
He was right in the middle of it.

sections.title: Chapter Sixteen - He Cried Too
sections.html:
CHAPTER SIXTEEN

He Cried Too


JESUS CRIED.

NOT just little sniffles.
Real tears.

He cried when his friend died.
He cried when people hurt.
He cried when no one understood him.

Even with all his power,
Even with all his love,
He still felt it all.

Happy Jesus wasn’t afraid to feel sad.
He let the tears come —
and he never told anyone else to hide theirs.

Because being soft…
was part of being strong.

sections.title: Chapter Seventeen - He Laughed, A Lot
sections.html:
CHAPTER SEVENTEEN

He Laughed, A Lot


JESUS LAUGHED.
LIKE, a lot.

He laughed at silly stories.
He laughed when kids made up wild games.
He laughed when someone tripped —
and then helped them up, still giggling.

He wasn’t stiff.
He wasn’t serious all the time.

He told jokes.
He smiled with his whole face.
He loved joy so much,
people followed him just to feel it.

Happy Jesus wasn’t just holy.
He was happy.

And that joy?
It’s still echoing.

sections.title: Chapter Eighteen - The Miracle Was Kindness
sections.html:
CHAPTER EIGHTEEN

The Miracle Was Kindness


JESUS DID BIG things.
Walked on water.
Healed the sick.
Fed thousands.

But the real miracle?
It wasn’t the magic.
It was the kindness.

The way he looked at people.
The way he listened.
The way he stayed soft in a world that wanted him hard.

That’s what changed things.
Not lightning from the sky —
but love from the heart.

Happy Jesus didn’t need a stage.
He just needed a moment…
to show someone they mattered.

sections.title: Chapter Nineteen - What Would Happy Jesus Do?
sections.html:
CHAPTER NINETEEN

What Would Happy Jesus Do?


WOULD HE YELL?
Would he brag?
Would he walk away?

Nope.

Happy Jesus would sit beside the kid with no friends.
He’d share his snacks.
He’d listen before speaking.
He’d laugh at your weird joke — even if it wasn’t funny.

He’d remind you that trying again is brave.
That saying sorry is strong.
That love is always worth it.

So the next time you wonder what to do…
Just ask:

“What would Happy Jesus do?”

Then do that.
Even if it’s small.
Even if it’s hard.

That’s how you change the world
without shouting.

sections.title: Chapter Twenty - The End (But Not Really)
sections.html:
CHAPTER TWENTY

The End (But Not Really)


THIS MIGHT BE the last page.
But it’s not the end.

Because Jesus didn’t stop smiling when the story was over.
And kindness didn’t stop mattering when the book closed.

Now it’s your turn.
To sit with someone.
To listen.
To forgive fast.
To be real.
To laugh loud.
To walk slow.
To love big.

Happy Jesus is still here.
Every time you choose love when it’s easier not to.

So yeah—this is the end.

But not really.

sections.title: About the Author
sections.html:
ABOUT THE AUTHOR


JJ IS A storyteller, sidewalk philosopher, and believer in second chances.
He writes books to make people cry, laugh, and think — sometimes all at once.
This is his 20-something-th book, but it might be his nicest.
He also believes Jesus would’ve laughed at fart jokes.

More at his Instagram: jj_james.johnson
